title: The invisible stylesheet
prompt:
A student team deploys its event registration website. The page opens and all headings and form fields are visible, but the layout has lost its colours, spacing and fonts. Reloading the page does not help. In the browser developer tools, the HTML request succeeds while the request for /styles.css returns HTTP 404. The stylesheet link is still present in the HTML, and no stylesheet content appears in the response.

HTML loads, but the network panel reports 404 for /styles.css. What is the most likely cause?
choices: Incorrect stylesheet URL or missing deployed file
A selector with lower CSS specificity
A later rule overriding the text color
explanation: A 404 response means the requested resource was not found at that URL; inspect the stylesheet path and deployed file.
hint: Check whether the browser successfully downloaded the stylesheet before investigating CSS rules.

title: A button that does nothing
prompt:
A team adds a button to reveal the event rules. Their JavaScript runs immediately from a script placed in the document head, above the body. The button is written later in the HTML and has the exact ID used by the script. When the page first loads, getElementById returns null, so the listener cannot be attached. Running the same lookup manually after the page finishes loading successfully finds the button.

A script in the document head calls getElementById before the button markup is parsed. It receives null. What caused this?
choices: The button has a CSS display rule
The button uses a relative font size
The target element has not been parsed yet
explanation: The lookup runs before the element has been parsed. Defer the script or wait for the DOM to be ready.
hint: Compare the time the lookup runs with the time the browser creates the target element.

title: The endless counter
prompt:
A volunteer writes a small pseudocode program to print five numbered instructions. It sets i to 1 and enters a WHILE loop whose condition is i <= 5. Inside the loop, the program prints the current value of i and immediately checks the same condition again. During a trial run, the console keeps printing 1 and the program never reaches the statement after the loop. No input or asynchronous work is involved.

Pseudocode sets i = 1 and repeats WHILE i <= 5, printing i without changing it. Why does it never finish?
choices: PRINT converts the counter into text
The counter starts at one instead of zero
explanation: The loop condition remains true because i never changes. Increment the counter inside the loop.
hint: Trace the value used by the loop condition across two iterations.

title: Login query fails
prompt:
A college portal checks a username against a SQL database. The developer builds the query text by concatenating the raw username entered in the login form. Ordinary names appear to work, but names containing a quote can break the query. A reviewer points out that specially constructed input could also change the meaning of the SQL. The team needs a server-side construction that keeps user input separate from executable query syntax.

A SQL query uses WHERE username = userInput by directly concatenating raw user input. What should replace this unsafe construction?
choices: Checking input only in browser JavaScript
A parameterized query with bound input values
Changing the query from POST to GET
explanation: Binding values through query parameters separates user input from SQL syntax.
hint: Look for a solution that treats input as data rather than part of SQL syntax.

title: Missing JSON data
prompt:
A dashboard requests a participant profile from an API. The network panel shows a successful response containing valid JSON, including a name property. In the client code, the developer awaits response.text() and stores the result in a variable named result. Logging result shows the JSON characters, but reading result.name produces undefined. The API response is complete, and the request has no network or permission error.

A server sends valid JSON, but JavaScript uses response.text() and then accesses result.name. Why is name undefined?
choices: The response body was read as a string
The server must return XML for property access
Every JSON object must contain an id field
The request method must always be POST
explanation: response.text() returns a string. Parse JSON, for example using response.json(), before reading object properties.
hint: Consider the JavaScript type returned by the response-reading method.

title: One result too many
prompt:
A leaderboard stores exactly five entries in an array with indexes 0 through 4. A developer writes a loop starting at index 0 and continuing while the index is less than or equal to 5. The first five reads retrieve valid entries, but the sixth read reaches outside the array. The program then fails when it tries to use a property of that nonexistent entry. The array length does not change during the loop.

An array has indexes 0 through 4. A loop reads indexes 0 through 5 inclusive. What caused the invalid access?
choices: The first item is at index one
The array must contain six comments
The array stores numbers rather than strings
The loop includes an invalid final index
explanation: An array of five items has valid indexes 0–4. Reading index 5 exceeds the array bounds.
hint: Compare the largest valid index with the last index visited by the loop.

title: Local works, remote fails
prompt:
A team tests a web application on the laptop that runs its backend. The frontend calls http://localhost:5000/api and receives data correctly. After the frontend is deployed, another student opens it on a different computer and cannot load the data. The deployed JavaScript still contains the same localhost address. The original laptop is running, but the other student has no backend process listening on port 5000 on their own computer.

A deployed frontend calls http://localhost:5000/api. Why can another student not reach the backend?
choices: Every frontend must use the database port directly
The HTTP method changes automatically after deployment
localhost refers to the visiting student’s own machine
React cannot send HTTP requests after deployment
explanation: localhost refers to the machine making the request, not the developer’s remote server.
hint: Think about which computer resolves the hostname in a browser request.

title: A locked-out user
prompt:
An event login system issues an access token with a valid signature and an expiry time of 16:00 UTC. A participant makes a request at 16:01 UTC and the server rejects it. The server clock is correct, the token has not been altered, and the same token worked before 16:00. The participant assumes that a valid signature should be enough to keep access open, but the system checks the configured time window as well.

An access token is configured to expire at 16:00 UTC. At 16:01 UTC the server rejects it even though the signature is valid. Which explanation matches these facts?
choices: The database has converted the email into a number
The configured access window has expired
The password must be typed in uppercase after noon
The login form needs a different font
explanation: The stated expiration time has passed. Valid credentials can still be rejected outside their configured access window.
hint: A token signature and a token expiry are separate checks.

title: Unexpected total
prompt:
A calculator reads two values from text inputs. The user enters 2 and 3, expecting the displayed sum to be 5. Debugging shows that the values stored by the program are the strings "2" and "3". The operation joins those strings and displays "23". Both input fields contain valid numeric text, so the team wants to change how these values are handled before performing addition.

A program reads the strings "2" and "3" and joins them into "23". What is needed to calculate 5?
choices: Convert both inputs to numeric values before addition
Append another plus sign to the result
Convert the final text to uppercase
explanation: Numeric-looking strings must be converted to numbers before numeric addition; otherwise joining them yields text.
hint: Inspect the types of the two operands before applying the operator.

title: Stale screen
prompt:
An organizer changes a team score on the server. A fresh API request returns the updated score, but a participant who already has the leaderboard open continues to see the old value. The page fetched its data once when it loaded and stored that response in local application state. It has no polling timer, subscription or refresh action. Refreshing the whole browser page immediately displays the updated score.

The server has a new score, but the page fetched scores only on initial load. What is missing?
choices: The SQL table must be deleted and recreated
The score must be rendered in an image element
The page must disable all HTTP caching forever
The page needs a refresh or live update mechanism
explanation: A one-time fetch is a snapshot. Fetch again, poll, or use a push update when the underlying score changes.
hint: Ask how new server data would reach the already-open page.

title: Repeated registrations
prompt:
Two students submit registration forms for the same email at nearly the same instant. Each server request first checks whether the email exists, and both checks find no existing row. Both requests then insert a new registration, leaving a duplicate. The team needs a database rule that remains effective when requests arrive concurrently, regardless of how many browsers or server processes are involved.

Two requests create a registration for the same email simultaneously. Which database control reliably prevents duplicates?
choices: Checking for duplicates only before INSERT in app code
A UNIQUE constraint on the email column
Disabling the submit button in only one browser
explanation: A database unique constraint rejects a conflicting email even when two insert requests race.
hint: The protection needs to work even if two checks run before either insert.

title: Unreachable website
prompt:
A student enters the event website domain and receives a DNS NXDOMAIN response before any web page loads. Other websites work normally on the same network. The browser never reaches the event server to request HTML or CSS. The organizer recently changed the domain setup and wants to choose the first area to investigate, using the network error rather than changing unrelated application code.

A domain lookup returns NXDOMAIN while other sites work. What should you investigate first?
explanation: NXDOMAIN says the queried domain name does not exist in DNS. Check the domain spelling and DNS setup first.
hint: Identify which network step happens before an HTTP request.

title: Form reload
prompt:
A registration form has a JavaScript submit listener that validates the fields and starts a custom request. The listener runs, but the browser then performs the form’s normal navigation as well, reloading the page and interrupting the intended interaction. There is no second click handler or duplicate listener. The developer needs to stop the default browser action for this submission while keeping the custom handler.

A JavaScript submit handler runs, but the browser performs a normal form submission too. What is missing?
choices: A return statement in an unrelated function
An additional CSS class on the form
explanation: Calling preventDefault() in the submit event handler prevents the browser’s default form submission.
hint: An event listener does not automatically cancel the browser’s built-in action.

title: Counting empty results
prompt:
A server endpoint runs a SQL lookup for a registration. When a record exists, rows[0].name displays the expected name. For an email that has never registered, the database correctly returns an empty result list. The application still tries to read rows[0].name and fails before it can display a helpful message. The database connection and SQL syntax are working correctly.

A query returns no rows, but code immediately reads rows[0].name. What is the issue?
choices: SQL guarantees one row for every SELECT
The name column is always a numeric type
The browser cannot render an empty table
The code accesses the first result without an empty-result check
explanation: The program must handle an empty result before dereferencing its first element.
hint: Consider what the first element of an empty result list would be.

title: A cross-origin request
prompt:
A frontend hosted on one origin requests data from a backend on another origin. The backend endpoint works when opened directly, but the browser blocks the frontend JavaScript from reading the response. Developer tools report that the frontend origin is not allowed by the backend’s cross-origin response policy. The team controls the backend and wants to permit this specific frontend to make the request.

A browser blocks a frontend request to a different backend origin because the backend does not allow that origin. What should be configured?
choices: The order of rows in the database
The backend CORS allowlist for the frontend origin
explanation: The backend must return CORS permission for the requesting frontend origin; CSS changes cannot grant it.
hint: This restriction is enforced by the browser using the server’s response headers.
